reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining Forsage through profit sharing and a one-time investment, while linking the enrollment of another person to instant wallet money and earnings from up-line, down-line, and cross-line participation. The “INSTANT MONEY” visual reinforces the immediate-return claim, although the records do not establish the investment amount, payment recipient, actual returns, or completed transactions.

citations.quote: Why join Forsage company
whenever you enroll someone instant money comes in your wallet
if you work here you earn money if you don't work you also earn money because here money comes from up, down line and cross line
company is the only company which has 100% profit sharing
if you have a question in mind that why to join 4th starts company

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker calls this a set of reasons to join [1], but the record leaves important financial terms undefined. “100% profit sharing” does not specify an individual payout, a timeframe, or how profits are calculated [2]. Even the claim that enrollment brings money to a wallet supplies no amount or evidence of a completed payment [3]. Those omissions do not make the claims reliable; they mean the video alone cannot establish what a participant would actually receive. Treat the claims as unverified, not as proof that a particular promised return was delivered or even precisely specified.

citations.quote: I am going to tell you 5 reasons
company is the only company which has 100% profit sharing
whenever you enroll someone instant money comes in your wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies an enrollment claim [1] and a claimed source of earnings across the network [2]. Neither quote establishes an investment amount, a payment recipient, or an actual return to anyone. “100% profit sharing” [3] likewise leaves the underlying calculation unexplained. The specific mechanism alleged is described in promotional terms, but the record does not verify how it operates.

citations.quote: whenever you enroll someone instant money comes in your wallet
money comes from up, down line and cross line
100% profit sharing

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is what the video promotes, not whether a viewer has already been paid. It offers immediate wallet money for enrolling someone [1] and says money comes from up-, down-, and cross-line positions even without work [2]. Unspecified amounts and unverified returns do not soften that recruitment-based earnings pitch; they leave viewers with fewer grounds to assess it.

citations.quote: whenever you enroll someone instant money comes in your wallet
if you work here you earn money if you don't work you also earn money because here money comes from up, down line and cross line

opening.argument: Judge, there is an explanatory reading of this presentation. Its stated subject is what Forsage is [1], and the description calls it a “business full plan” [2]. The speaker describes where money supposedly comes from within the arrangement [3] and says it is based on blockchain technology [4]. Those statements can be assessed as an account of a claimed business model without accepting them as true. The supplied speech does not give a sign-up procedure or a destination for sending funds. Calling the explanation unreliable would be fair; treating the explanation itself as evidence of a completed solicitation goes further than this record supports.

citations.quote: What is Forsage company
Forsage business full plan
here money comes from up, down line and cross line
It based on blockchain technology

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening is right that the speaker gives reasons to join [1]. But its cited network language [2] also describes the arrangement's claimed operation; it does not show an enrollment being carried out. The title pairs the join question with “What is Forsage company” [3]. The judge can recognize promotional wording while still distinguishing a discussion of claims from evidence that funds were requested or transferred.

citations.quote: Why join Forsage company
money comes from up, down line and cross line
What is Forsage company

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The explanatory framing omits the speaker's purpose: he says he is giving reasons that would persuade someone to join [1]. One of those reasons is instant wallet money upon enrolling another person [2]; another is income even without working, attributed to up-, down-, and cross-line participation [3]. No completed transfer is needed to identify a promotional recruitment pitch.

citations.quote: if you have a question in mind that why to join 4th starts company so I am going to tell you 5 reasons which would not stop you after you hear this
whenever you enroll someone instant money comes in your wallet
if you don't work you also earn money because here money comes from up, down line and cross line

opening.argument: Judge, the enrollment statement can be read as a referral reward: when someone enrolls another person, money is said to arrive in a wallet [1]. Referral incentives alone do not establish deception. The speaker also uses the language of profit sharing [2], but gives no amount that a viewer must pay, no payment destination, and no evidence of a completed transaction. The mention of up-, down-, and cross-line money [3] raises a serious question about the structure; it does not, by itself, show the precise terms under which any participant is paid. On this limited record, the mechanism remains insufficiently specified to conclude that the advertised reward is fraudulent.

citations.quote: whenever you enroll someone instant money comes in your wallet
company is the only company which has 100% profit sharing
money comes from up, down line and cross line

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the enrollment reward [1] and network earnings [2] as decisive. They establish what the speaker claims, but not the terms of a deposit, who would receive one, or whether the claimed wallet payment occurs. Even the investment reference says only that it is a type of investment [3]. Those gaps matter when distinguishing an asserted referral arrangement from a demonstrated fraudulent transaction.

citations.quote: whenever you enroll someone instant money comes in your wallet
money comes from up, down line and cross line
It have a type investment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not presented merely as a reward for one ordinary referral. The speaker promises wallet money when someone is enrolled [1] and says participants earn even when they do not work because money comes from up-, down-, and cross-line positions [2]. The investment language [3] adds to the financial pitch. Missing transaction details limit what can be said about actual payments, but they do not erase the recruitment-and-tier structure being promoted.
